facts.statement: In 2008, Daxiatitan was considered potentially the largest known dinosaur found in China.
facts.quote: At the time of its discovery in 2008, Daxiatitan was regarded as potentially the largest known dinosaur from China.

facts.statement: Daxiatitan lived during the Lower Cretaceous period in Gansu, China.
facts.quote: Daxiatitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur known from the Lower Cretaceous of Gansu, China.

facts.statement: The genus Daxiatitan and its species D. binglingi were named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, Zhou Lingqi, and Ji Qiang in 2008.
facts.quote: Daxiatitan and its type and only species Daxiatitan binglingi were named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, Zhou Lingqi, and Ji Qiang in 2008.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Daxia River, and the species name refers to Bingling Temple, both located in the region where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the Daxia River, a tributary of the Yellow River that runs through the area where the type specimen was found, and the species name refers to Bingling Temple, which is located in the region.

facts.statement: A 2020 study suggested that Daxiatitan and Euhelopus might form a clade with mamenchisaurids.
facts.quote: In 2020, a phylogenetic analysis conducted by Moore et al. found that Daxiatitan and Euhelopus may form a clade with mamenchisaurids.

facts.statement: Daxiatitan is estimated to have been 23 to 30 meters long and weighed 23 tonnes.
facts.quote: Its length has been estimated as 23 – 30 meters, and its mass has been estimated as 23 tonnes.

facts.statement: Daxiatitan had an estimated neck length of approximately 12 meters, placing it among the sauropods with longer necks.
facts.quote: The neck of Daxiatitan is estimated to have been approximately 12 m long, making it among the longer-necked sauropods

facts.statement: Daxiatitan lived approximately 135 million years ago during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 135 millones de años, en el Valanginiense

facts.statement: Like Euhelopus and Huanghetitan, Daxiatitan possessed an extremely long neck.
facts.quote: Como Euhelopus y Huanghetitan, tenía un cuello enormemente largo.

facts.statement: Daxiatitan is distinguished from other titanosaurs by having cervical vertebrae with cranial prezygapophyseal facets that compensate caudally, such that the non-articular bone covers the cranial portions of most prezygapophyses.
facts.quote: Se distingue de los otros titanosaurianos por poseer vértebras cervicales con facetas prezygapofisiales craneales se compensan en caudal tal que el hueso no articular abarca las porciones craneales de la mayoría del prezygapofisis.

facts.statement: Daxiatitan is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria.
The time range for Daxiatitan is estimated from 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Daxiatitan is identified as Euhelopodidae.

rejected.statement: The known remains of Daxiatitan include a partial skeleton with most neck and back vertebrae, two tail vertebrae, a shoulder blade, and a thigh bone.
rejected.quote: It is known from a single partial skeleton consisting of most of the neck and back vertebrae, two tail vertebrae, a shoulder blade, and a thigh bone.
